rules.legal_concept: Resident right to inspect and copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Every Alabama resident has a right to inspect and take a copy of any public record of the state, except as otherwise expressly provided by applicable law; the right (and the corresponding duty to respond under the procedural sections) runs to residents, not to any person.
rules.trigger: A resident seeks to inspect or copy a public record
rules.source_language: Every resident has a right to inspect and take a copy of any public record of this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by applicable law.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-40(a) (amended by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess., eff. Oct. 1, 2024)
rules.notes: 2024 amendment replaced 'citizen' with 'resident' throughout, narrowing standing. Enrolled PDF shows amendatory markup ('citizenresident'); quoted text is the enacted operative clause. Alabama therefore has a residency requirement (contrast eligibility.any_person / eligibility.no_residency_requirement used by open-access states).

rules.legal_concept: Definition of RESIDENT
rules.atomic_rule: 'Resident' means an individual permanently domiciled in Alabama with an expectation to remain, as demonstrated by reasonable proof of residency such as an Alabama driver license or voter registration; the software branches request eligibility on this definition.
rules.trigger: Determining whether a requester qualifies as a resident
rules.source_language: RESIDENT. An individual who is permanently domiciled in Alabama with an expectation to remain in Alabama as demonstrated by reasonable proof of residency such as, but not limited to, an Alabama driver license or voter registration.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(3) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Definition the platform branches on for the residency gate.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: The right to inspect and copy is granted to every resident without any condition that the requester state or justify a purpose; no statement of purpose is required to make a request.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every resident has a right to inspect and take a copy of any public record of this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by applicable law.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-40(a) (amended by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry key: emitted as an affirmative rule (not a material negative). The grant is unconditional as to purpose; no purpose-of-use condition appears anywhere in Article 36-12. The prescribed request form (AL-0019) likewise asks only for residency standing, not purpose.

rules.legal_concept: Public officer may require proof of residency
rules.atomic_rule: A public officer may request reasonable evidence from the requester to establish proof of residency.
rules.trigger: A request is received and the officer seeks to verify residency
rules.source_language: A public officer may request reasonable evidence to establish proof of residency.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(f) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Discretionary intake verification step.

rules.legal_concept: Discretion to respond to nonresidents
rules.atomic_rule: A public officer has discretion to respond to public records requests made by nonresidents; responding to one nonresident request does not waive the officer's right to deny other or future nonresident requests.
rules.trigger: A request is made by a nonresident
rules.source_language: A public officer shall have the discretion to respond to public records requests made by nonresidents, in which case, a public officer's decision to respond to such requests shall not operate as a waiver of the public officer's right to deny other or future requests made by nonresidents.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(f) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Routing/classification fork: nonresident requests are handled at the officer's discretion rather than as of right.

rules.legal_concept: Judicial branch and Article VI offices exempt from procedural sections
rules.atomic_rule: The judicial branch of state government and any office identified in Article VI of the Constitution of Alabama of 2022 are exempt from the request-processing requirements of Sections 36-12-43 through 36-12-45; requests to those bodies do not follow the standard/time-intensive procedural tracks.
rules.trigger: Request is directed to the judicial branch or an Article VI office
rules.source_language: For purposes of this article, the judicial branch of state government and any office identified in Article VI of the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, are exempted from the requirements of Sections 36-12-43 through 36-12-45.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-40(b) (amended by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Coverage carve-out from the procedural machinery. Municipal governments and other public officers remain covered (the Act's chief purpose; RFD County and Municipal Government).

rules.legal_concept: Definition of BUSINESS DAY
rules.atomic_rule: A 'business day' is a day the public officer's office is open to the public and conducting normal operations; the engine uses this to count all business-day deadlines.
rules.trigger: Counting any business-day deadline
rules.source_language: BUSINESS DAY. A day that the public officer's office is open to the public and conducting normal operations.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(1) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Calculation basis; office-specific (varies per public officer's operating calendar).

rules.legal_concept: Definition of PUBLIC OFFICER
rules.atomic_rule: 'Public officer' means a public officer or his or her designee responsible for responding to public records requests; this identifies who must respond and to whom requests route.
rules.trigger: Determining who is responsible for responding
rules.source_language: PUBLIC OFFICER. A public officer or his or her designee responsible for responding to public records requests.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Custodian designation / who-must-respond keeper-sliver; drives routing and permits designee handling (e.g., a public records coordinator per 36-12-45(a)(1)b).

rules.legal_concept: Definition of STANDARD REQUEST
rules.atomic_rule: A 'standard request' is one that seeks specifically and discretely identified records the public officer determines would take less than eight hours of staff time to process (identifying, retrieving, and redacting/withholding protected information), requiring no or minimal clarification; it routes to the standard-request track.
rules.trigger: Officer estimates processing time at less than 8 staff hours
rules.source_language: STANDARD REQUEST. A public records request that seeks one or more specifically and discretely identified public records that the public officer determines would take less than eight hours of staff time to process considering the time needed to identify and retrieve any responsive records and to redact or take other measures to withhold protected information. A standard request should require no or minimal clarification by the requester.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: The 8-hour figure is a fixed statutory threshold; the classification forks the workflow into two tracks (structural). Determination is committed to the public officer's judgment.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of TIME-INTENSIVE REQUEST
rules.atomic_rule: A 'time-intensive request' is one the public officer determines would take more than eight hours of staff time to process (identifying, retrieving, and redacting/withholding protected information); it routes to the time-intensive track.
rules.trigger: Officer estimates processing time at more than 8 staff hours
rules.source_language: TIME-INTENSIVE REQUEST. A public records request that the public officer determines would take more than eight hours of staff time to process considering the time needed to identify and retrieve any responsive records and any time needed to redact or take other measures to withhold protected information.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(6) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: 8-hour fixed statutory threshold; forks to the time-intensive track.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of SUBSTANTIVE RESPONSE
rules.atomic_rule: A 'substantive response' is a response setting forth the public officer's ultimate position on the substance of the request; it includes (in whole or part) providing the records, stating access will be provided at a set/agreed time and place, stating records are ready upon payment of a reasonable fee, or a denial with reasons, on the ground the record does not exist, for failure to substantially complete the request form, for failure to comply with written procedures, or because the records are not public.
rules.trigger: Officer states its ultimate position on a request
rules.source_language: SUBSTANTIVE RESPONSE. A response to a proper public records request that sets forth the public officer's ultimate position on the substance of the request. The term includes, but is not limited to, the following, in whole or in part: a. A statement that the public records are provided as attached or enclosed. b. A statement that access to the requested public records will be provided at a set time, place, and location during regular business hours or at a time, place, and location mutually agreeable to the public officer and the requester. c. A statement that the public officer is prepared to provide the requested public records to the requester upon payment of a reasonable fee. d. A statement that denies the request with reasons stated therefor. e. A statement that denies the request on the grounds that the requested public record does not exist within the government agency. If known to the public officer, the public officer may identify the proper custodian or location for the requested public record. f. A statement that denies the request for failure to substantially complete a standard request form. g. A statement that denies the request for failure to substantially comply with the written procedures established by the public officer for such request. h. A statement that denies the request because the records sought are not public.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(5) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Terminal event definition: providing a 'substantive response' is what satisfies the response deadlines and rebuts the constructive-denial presumption. Enumerated denial grounds (d-h) and the custodian-referral (e) are captured separately as AL-0048 and AL-0050.

rules.legal_concept: Requesting via public officer's written procedures
rules.atomic_rule: A resident may request access to a public record by following the written procedures established by the public officer having custody; those procedures may set a standard form, a designated recipient (e.g., a public records coordinator), permissible transmission methods, and other submission policies.
rules.trigger: Resident initiates a request where the officer has adopted written procedures
rules.source_language: A resident may request access to a public record by following the written procedures for accepting such requests established by the public officer having custody of the public record. The written procedures may establish any of the following: a. A standard request form for use in submitting a public records request. b. A designee, such as a public records coordinator, to whom a public records request shall be addressed. c. The permissible method or methods of transmitting a public records request. d. Any other policies pertaining to the process for submitting a public records request.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(a)(1) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Written procedures need not be adopted as administrative rules under the Alabama APA (36-12-45(a)(4)).

rules.legal_concept: Written procedures made reasonably available
rules.atomic_rule: The public officer shall make its written procedures concerning public records reasonably available to the public.
rules.trigger: Public officer has adopted written procedures
rules.source_language: The public officer shall make his or her written procedures concerning public records reasonably available to the public.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(a)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)

rules.legal_concept: No obligation to respond to requests not made per procedures
rules.atomic_rule: A public officer is not obligated to respond to a public records request that is not made pursuant to the officer's written procedures.
rules.trigger: Request does not follow the officer's written procedures
rules.source_language: A public officer shall not be obligated to respond to a public records request that is not made pursuant to the public officer's written procedures.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(a)(3) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Gates whether the response clocks start at all.

rules.legal_concept: Standard request may require form/procedures (standard track)
rules.atomic_rule: For a standard request, the public officer may require the requester to submit using a standard request form or by following the officer's written procedures for accepting requests.
rules.trigger: Standard request received
rules.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to submit his or her request using a standard request form or by following the written procedures for accepting requests for public records established by the public officer.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(1) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Permissive ('may') for standard requests; contrast AL-0016 (mandatory 'shall' for time-intensive).

rules.legal_concept: Standard form/procedures required (time-intensive track)
rules.atomic_rule: For a time-intensive request, the public officer shall require the requester to submit using a standard request form or by following the officer's written procedures for accepting requests.
rules.trigger: Time-intensive request received
rules.source_language: The public officer shall require the requester to submit his or her request using a standard request form or by following the written procedures for accepting requests for public records established by the public officer.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(1) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Mandatory for time-intensive requests.

rules.legal_concept: Default submission method absent written procedures
rules.atomic_rule: In the absence of written procedures to the contrary, a resident may submit a request by hand-delivering it or mailing it to the main office or principal place of business of the public officer having custody of the record.
rules.trigger: Public officer has no written procedures
rules.source_language: In the absence of written procedures to the contrary, each of the following shall apply: (1) A resident may submit a public records request by delivering the request by hand or by mailing the request to the main office or principal place of business of the public officer having custody of the public record.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(b)(1) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Default-path fork used only where the officer has not adopted procedures.

rules.legal_concept: When receipt of a request occurs
rules.atomic_rule: Receipt of a hand-delivered request occurs when it is received at the officer's main office or principal place of business; receipt of a mailed request occurs on the date of actual receipt by the officer; a certified-mail or similar signed postage receipt is prima facie evidence of receipt.
rules.trigger: A request is delivered by hand or mail (absent contrary procedures)
rules.source_language: Receipt of a hand-delivered public records request occurs when the request is received at the public officer's main office or principal place of business. Receipt of a mailed public records request occurs on the date of actual receipt by the public officer. A certified mail receipt or similar signed postage receipt shall be prima facie evidence of receipt by the public officer.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Anchors the start event ('receiving the request') for the acknowledgment clock; not itself a deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Prescribed standard request form and residency certification
rules.atomic_rule: The standard request form shall read substantially as the statutory form (requester contact info, agency, date, and records requested), and the requester, by submitting, certifies being an Alabama resident with standing to request; the officer may require additional information or reorder/reformat fields.
rules.trigger: A standard request form is used or provided
rules.source_language: The standard request form shall read substantially as follows, provided a public officer may require additional information or modify the order or format in which the information is requested: "Requester's contact information: Name... Phone number... Email address... Street address... City... State... Zip... Agency you are requesting public records from... Date of request... Records requested: (Be as specific as possible...) ... Payment of fees may be required before your request is fulfilled. By submitting this request, you certify that you are an Alabama resident with standing to make a request for public records pursuant to Alabama law."
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(b)(3) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Source language condensed to the form's field labels and the certification sentence (form field lines are blanks). The certification asks only for residency standing, not purpose.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable specificity; no duty for vague or overbroad requests
rules.atomic_rule: A request shall identify the requested public record with reasonable specificity, and a public officer is not obligated to respond to a request that is vague, ambiguous, overly broad, or unreasonable in scope.
rules.trigger: Request lacks reasonable specificity or is overly broad
rules.source_language: A request made pursuant to this article shall identify the requested public record with reasonable specificity. A public officer shall not be obligated to respond to a public records request that is vague, ambiguous, overly broad, or unreasonable in scope.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(c) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: 'Reasonable specificity' / 'overly broad' are undefined standards, preserved verbatim.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: A public officer is not required to create a new public record if the requested record does not already exist.
rules.trigger: Requested record does not already exist
rules.source_language: A public officer shall not be required to create a new public record if the requested record does not already exist.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(d) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)

rules.legal_concept: No duty to respond to requests for non-records
rules.atomic_rule: A public officer is not required to respond to requests that seek information or other materials that are not public records.
rules.trigger: Request seeks information/materials that are not public records
rules.source_language: A public officer shall not be required to respond to requests that seek information or other materials that are not public records.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(e) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Distinguishes records requests from requests for information/answers.

rules.legal_concept: Clarification tolls and restarts timelines
rules.atomic_rule: If a public officer responds by seeking clarification or additional information, the timelines are tolled and restart once the officer receives the requested clarification/information, as if the requester had submitted a new request.
rules.trigger: Officer seeks clarification or additional information
rules.clock_spec: Timelines tolled on request for clarification; restart from zero upon receipt of clarification/additional information (treated as a new request)
rules.source_language: If a public officer responds to a request by seeking clarification or additional information, the timelines established in this section shall be tolled and shall restart once the public officer receives the requested clarification or additional information as if the requester had submitted a new request. A public officer's decision to seek clarification or additional information with respect to any particular request shall not operate as a waiver of the public officer's right to seek clarification or additional information in response to other, future requests.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(g) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Statute says both 'tolled' and 'restart ... as if a new request'; effect is a full restart of all timelines from receipt of clarification, not a mere pause.

rules.legal_concept: Acknowledgment deadline (standard request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a standard request, the public officer shall acknowledge a proper request within 10 days of receiving the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a proper standard request
rules.clock_spec: 10 days from receipt of the request
rules.source_language: The public officer shall acknowledge a proper request within 10 days of receiving the request.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(3) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Standard track says '10 days' (calendar), whereas the time-intensive acknowledgment (AL-0030) says '10 business days' — the unit differs between tracks in the enacted text.

rules.legal_concept: Substantive response deadline (standard request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a standard request, the public officer shall provide a substantive response fulfilling or denying a proper request within 15 business days of acknowledging receipt.
rules.trigger: Acknowledgment of receipt of a standard request
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from acknowledgment of receipt
rules.source_language: The public officer shall provide a substantive response fulfilling or denying a proper request within 15 business days of acknowledging receipt.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Accompanied by an aspirational 'as expeditiously as possible' standard (advisory 'should'), not a separate deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Extension of standard response period
rules.atomic_rule: The public officer may extend the standard substantive-response period in 15-business-day increments upon written notice to the requester.
rules.trigger: Officer needs more time and gives written notice
rules.clock_spec: +15 business-days per written extension notice (repeatable increments)
rules.source_language: Although the public officer may extend this period in 15-business-day increments upon written notice to the requester, the public officer should process a standard request as expeditiously as possible considering the requester's time constraints, the public officer's workload, and the nature of the request.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: No stated cap on number of increments, but the constructive-denial outer bound (AL-0027) still applies. The 15-business-day increment is the fixed parameter.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive (deemed) denial — standard request, no response
rules.atomic_rule: There is a rebuttable presumption that a proper standard request has been denied if a substantive response is not provided within the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days following acknowledgment of receipt.
rules.trigger: No substantive response by the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days after acknowledgment
rules.clock_spec: Earlier of 30 business-days or 60 calendar-days from acknowledgment of receipt
rules.source_language: There shall be a rebuttable presumption that a proper standard request has been denied by the public officer if: a. A substantive response is not provided to the standard request within the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days following acknowledgment of receipt by the public officer;
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(5)a (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Deemed-denial keeper-sliver: trigger captured, remedy (mandamus/damages) not. Presumption is rebuttable and subject to the no-presumption carve-outs (AL-0029).

rules.legal_concept: Constructive denial — standard request, records not produced after payment
rules.atomic_rule: There is a rebuttable presumption that a proper standard request has been denied if the public records are not produced within the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days following payment of the estimated fees to the public officer.
rules.trigger: Records not produced by the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days after fee payment
rules.clock_spec: Earlier of 30 business-days or 60 calendar-days from payment of estimated fees
rules.source_language: b. The public records are not produced within the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days following the payment of the estimated fees to the public officer.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(5)b (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Second constructive-denial trigger, keyed to the post-payment production clock.

rules.legal_concept: No constructive-denial presumption (standard request)
rules.atomic_rule: No presumption of denial arises for a standard request if the request is not proper or the officer is not obligated to respond, the officer has responded in part, the officer and requester have agreed on the time or substance of the response, negotiations are ongoing, or the officer has reasonably communicated the request's status.
rules.trigger: Any listed circumstance is present
rules.source_language: There shall be no presumption that a proper standard request has been denied if: a. The request is not proper or the public officer is not obligated or required to respond as provided in this section; b. The public officer has responded in part; c. The public officer and requester have reached an agreement regarding the time or substance, or both, of the response; d. Negotiations are ongoing between the public officer and the requester; or e. The public officer has reasonably communicated the status of the request to the requester.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(6) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Conjunctive list of carve-outs; kept in one row. 'Reasonably communicated the status' can indefinitely defer the deemed-denial clock.

rules.legal_concept: Acknowledgment deadline (time-intensive request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a time-intensive request, the public officer shall acknowledge the request within 10 business days of receiving the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a time-intensive request
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of the request
rules.source_language: The public officer shall acknowledge the request within 10 business days of receiving the request.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(3) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Same concept as AL-0024 but time-intensive track uses '10 business days' (vs '10 days' for standard). At intake the track is not yet known; classification notice follows within 15 business days (AL-0031).

rules.legal_concept: Notice that request qualifies as time-intensive
rules.atomic_rule: The public officer shall notify the requester within 15 business days after acknowledging receipt that the request qualifies as a time-intensive request, and shall at that time notify the requester of any likely fees.
rules.trigger: Officer determines request is time-intensive
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from acknowledgment of receipt
rules.source_language: The public officer shall notify the requester within 15 business days after acknowledging receipt that the request qualifies as a time-intensive request. At that time, the public officer shall notify the requester of any likely fees and allow the requester to withdraw the time-intensive request and submit a new request that is not a time-intensive request.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Atomic split of 36-12-44(b)(4): this row = the classification-notice deadline and likely-fee notice. Withdrawal option is AL-0032; 45-day response window is AL-0033; extension is AL-0034.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may withdraw and resubmit as non-time-intensive
rules.atomic_rule: Upon the time-intensive designation notice, the officer shall allow the requester to withdraw the time-intensive request and submit a new request that is not time-intensive; the requester may instead elect to proceed.
rules.trigger: Requester receives the time-intensive designation notice
rules.source_language: At that time, the public officer shall notify the requester of any likely fees and allow the requester to withdraw the time-intensive request and submit a new request that is not a time-intensive request. If the requester elects to proceed with a time-intensive request, the public officer shall provide a substantive response...
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Branch/state: the requester's election to proceed is also the start event for the 45-business-day response clock (AL-0033).

rules.legal_concept: Substantive response deadline (time-intensive request)
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester elects to proceed with a time-intensive request, the public officer shall provide a substantive response fulfilling or denying the request within 45 business days after the requester elected to proceed.
rules.trigger: Requester elects to proceed with a time-intensive request
rules.clock_spec: 45 business-days from the requester's election to proceed
rules.source_language: If the requester elects to proceed with a time-intensive request, the public officer shall provide a substantive response fulfilling or denying the request within 45 business days after the requester elected to proceed with his or her time-intensive request.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Clock start is the requester's election to proceed, not acknowledgment.

rules.legal_concept: Extension of time-intensive response period
rules.atomic_rule: The public officer may extend the 45-business-day time-intensive response period in 45-business-day increments by notifying the requester in writing.
rules.trigger: Officer needs more time and gives written notice
rules.clock_spec: +45 business-days per written extension notice (repeatable increments)
rules.source_language: The public officer may extend this period in 45-business-day increments by notifying the requester in writing.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: No stated cap on increments, but the constructive-denial outer bound (AL-0036) applies.

rules.legal_concept: Confidential log of pending time-intensive requests
rules.atomic_rule: At or around the time of designating a request as time-intensive, the public officer shall record it in a log of currently pending time-intensive requests identifying the requester's name and the date of acknowledgment; the log is confidential and not subject to disclosure under this article (though it may remain discoverable under applicable procedure rules).
rules.trigger: A request is designated time-intensive
rules.source_language: At or around the time of designating the request as time-intensive, the public officer shall make a record in a log maintained for keeping track of currently pending time-intensive requests. For each such currently pending request, the log shall identify the name of the requester and the date of acknowledgment pursuant to subdivision (3). The log shall be a confidential document that is not subject to disclosure pursuant to this article, provided the log may remain discoverable pursuant to proper discovery methods provided under applicable rules of procedure.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(5) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Legally required request tracking (kept because mandated); the log itself is a confidential record type.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive denial — time-intensive request, no response
rules.atomic_rule: There is a rebuttable presumption that a proper time-intensive request has been denied if a substantive response is not provided within the earlier of 180 business days or 270 calendar days following the requester's election to proceed.
rules.trigger: No substantive response by the earlier of 180 business days or 270 calendar days after election to proceed
rules.clock_spec: Earlier of 180 business-days or 270 calendar-days from election to proceed
rules.source_language: There shall be a rebuttable presumption that a proper time-intensive request has been denied by the public officer if: a. A substantive response is not provided within the earlier of 180 business days or 270 calendar days following the requester's election to proceed with a time-intensive request.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(6)a (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Time-intensive deemed-denial outer bound; same concept as AL-0027 with the time-intensive numbers.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive denial — time-intensive request, records not produced after payment
rules.atomic_rule: There is a rebuttable presumption that a proper time-intensive request has been denied if the records are not produced within the earlier of 180 business days or 270 calendar days following payment of the estimated fees to the public officer.
rules.trigger: Records not produced by the earlier of 180 business days or 270 calendar days after fee payment
rules.clock_spec: Earlier of 180 business-days or 270 calendar-days from payment of estimated fees
rules.source_language: b. The records are not produced within the earlier of 180 business days or 270 calendar days following the payment of the estimated fees to the public officer.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(6)b (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Post-payment production trigger for time-intensive requests.

rules.legal_concept: No constructive-denial presumption (time-intensive request)
rules.atomic_rule: No presumption of denial arises for a time-intensive request if the request is not proper or the officer is not obligated to respond, the officer has responded in part, the officer and requester have agreed on the time or substance of the response, negotiations are ongoing, or the officer has reasonably communicated the request's status.
rules.trigger: Any listed circumstance is present
rules.source_language: There shall be no presumption that a proper time-intensive request has been denied if: a. The request is not proper or the public officer is not obligated or required to respond as provided in this section; b. The public officer has responded in part; c. The public officer and requester have reached an agreement regarding the time or substance, or both, of the response; d. Negotiations are ongoing between the public officer and the requester; or e. The public officer has reasonably communicated the status of the request to the requester.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(7) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Mirror of AL-0029 for the time-intensive track.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee for records (standard request / general)
rules.atomic_rule: A public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records (standard request); more generally, a certified copy is furnished on payment of a reasonable fee.
rules.trigger: Officer elects to charge for a standard request
rules.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable fee ... set by the public officer' — soft-standard; the city/officer supplies the actual value (no statewide rate or per-page ceiling). Fees may increase for extensive requests per the prescribed form notice (36-12-45(b)(3)).

rules.legal_concept: Estimated-fee notice (standard request)
rules.atomic_rule: If the public officer elects to charge a fee for a standard request, the officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment.
rules.trigger: Officer elects to charge a fee for a standard request
rules.source_language: If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Conditional-on-charging notice duty for the standard track.

rules.legal_concept: Withhold records until payment (standard request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a standard request where a fee is charged, the public officer shall withhold any public records until receipt of payment.
rules.trigger: A fee has been charged and remains unpaid (standard request)
rules.source_language: If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Payment of estimated fees is the start event for the production constructive-denial clock (AL-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Requester may decline to pay
rules.atomic_rule: The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response (standard request).
rules.trigger: Requester declines to pay the estimated fee
rules.source_language: The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Terminal state a request can enter (requester abandons by non-payment).

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment before search (standard request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a standard request, the public officer has discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.
rules.trigger: Standard request where officer requires a deposit before searching
rules.source_language: Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Deposit/advance-payment gate before the search step.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory reasonable fee before response (time-intensive request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a time-intensive request, the public officer shall require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before providing a substantive response.
rules.trigger: Time-intensive request received
rules.source_language: The public officer shall require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before providing a substantive response to the requester.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: For time-intensive requests charging a fee is mandatory ('shall require'), unlike the permissive standard track (AL-0039). The fee amount remains the reasonable-fee soft standard.

rules.legal_concept: Advance likely-fee notice and withholding (time-intensive request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a time-intensive request, the public officer shall notify the requester in advance of any likely fees and shall withhold any substantive response until receipt of payment.
rules.trigger: Time-intensive request with likely fees
rules.source_language: The public officer shall notify the requester in advance of any likely fees and shall withhold any substantive response until receipt of payment.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Advance likely-fee notice also occurs at the time-intensive designation notice (AL-0031).

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment before search (time-intensive request)
rules.atomic_rule: For a time-intensive request, the public officer has discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.
rules.trigger: Time-intensive request where officer requires a deposit before searching
rules.source_language: Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Same concept as AL-0043 in the time-intensive track.

rules.legal_concept: Notice to infrastructure owner on critical-infrastructure requests
rules.atomic_rule: A public officer who receives a request that may appear to relate to critical infrastructure or critical energy infrastructure information shall notify the owner of such infrastructure in writing of the request and provide the owner an opportunity to comment on the request and on the threats to public safety or welfare that could reasonably be expected from public disclosure.
rules.trigger: Request may appear to relate to critical infrastructure or critical energy infrastructure information
rules.source_language: Any public officer who receives a request for records that may appear to relate to critical infrastructure or critical energy infrastructure information, shall notify the owner of such infrastructure in writing of the request and provide the owner an opportunity to comment on the request and on the threats to public safety or welfare that could reasonably be expected from public disclosure of the records.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-40(a) (amended by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Third-party owner-notice-and-comment branch that alters processing; tied to the critical-infrastructure/security exemption. 'Critical infrastructure' defined by 42 U.S.C. § 5195c(e); 'critical energy infrastructure information' by 18 C.F.R. § 388.113(c)(1). Flag for human legal review on scope.

rules.legal_concept: Denial states reasons
rules.atomic_rule: A response that denies a request must state the reasons for the denial (a denial 'with reasons stated therefor' is what counts as a substantive response denying the request).
rules.trigger: Officer denies a request on the merits
rules.source_language: A statement that denies the request with reasons stated therefor.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(5)d (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Extracted from the substantive-response definition (AL-0011); the statute lists reasoned denial as one qualifying substantive response. Other enumerated denial grounds (record does not exist, incomplete form, noncompliant with procedures, records not public) are in AL-0011.

rules.legal_concept: Referral to proper custodian when record does not exist
rules.atomic_rule: When denying a request because the requested public record does not exist within the agency, the public officer may, if known, identify the proper custodian or location for the requested record.
rules.trigger: Requested record does not exist within the agency
rules.source_language: A statement that denies the request on the grounds that the requested public record does not exist within the government agency. If known to the public officer, the public officer may identify the proper custodian or location for the requested public record.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(5)e (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Wrong-department routing keeper-sliver: permissive referral to the proper custodian.

rules.legal_concept: Arranged access for inspection
rules.atomic_rule: A substantive response may provide that access to the requested records will be given at a set time, place, and location during regular business hours, or at a time, place, and location mutually agreeable to the public officer and the requester.
rules.trigger: Officer grants access by inspection rather than copies
rules.source_language: A statement that access to the requested public records will be provided at a set time, place, and location during regular business hours or at a time, place, and location mutually agreeable to the public officer and the requester.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(5)b (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Production-mode option: in-person inspection during business hours or at a mutually agreeable time.

rules.legal_concept: Certified copy on request upon reasonable fee
rules.atomic_rule: Every public officer having custody of a public record a resident has a right to inspect shall, on proper request, provide a certified copy of the record on payment of a reasonable fee, and such copy is admissible as evidence like the original.
rules.trigger: Resident makes a proper request for a certified copy and pays the reasonable fee
rules.source_language: Every public officer having the custody of a public record that a resident has a right to inspect shall provide him or her, on proper request as provided in this article, with a certified copy of the public record, on payment of a reasonable fee, as further provided in this article, and such copy is admissible as evidence in like cases and with like effect as the original writing.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-41 (amended by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Enrolled PDF shows amendatory markup; quoted text is the enacted operative clause (old 'citizen'/'legal fees'/'demand' replaced by 'resident'/'reasonable fee'/'proper request').

rules.legal_concept: Records request not a substitute for discovery
rules.atomic_rule: The article shall not be construed to permit any party to a pending or threatened action, suit, or proceeding to obtain information relevant to that matter in lieu of the proper discovery methods provided under applicable rules of procedure.
rules.trigger: Requester is a party to a pending or threatened action seeking matter-relevant information
rules.source_language: Nothing in this article shall be construed to permit any party to a pending or threatened action, suit, or proceeding to obtain information regarding a matter relevant to the pending or threatened action, suit, or proceeding in lieu of the proper discovery methods provided under applicable rules of procedure.
rules.source_authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-46 (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
rules.notes: Routes/blocks litigation-driven requests to the discovery process; flag for human legal review on application.

structural_branches.description: Two-track processing fork: requests estimated at <8 staff hours run the standard track (AL-0009).
Requests estimated at >8 staff hours run the separate time-intensive track with its own longer timeline (AL-0010).

After the time-intensive designation notice, the request branches: requester may withdraw and resubmit a non-time-intensive request, or elect to proceed (which starts the 45-business-day clock) (AL-0032).
Seeking clarification/additional information tolls all timelines and restarts them from zero on receipt, as if a new request (AL-0023).
Judicial branch and Article VI constitutional offices are routed out of the 36-12-43 through 36-12-45 procedural machinery (AL-0006).
Requests touching critical infrastructure trigger a mandatory written notice-and-comment branch to the infrastructure owner before disposition (AL-0047).
Non-existent-record denials may branch to a referral identifying the proper custodian/location (AL-0049).
Absent adopted written procedures, the engine falls back to a statutory default submission path (hand/mail to main office) and receipt-determination rules (AL-0017, AL-0018).
Deemed-denial presumption can be suspended indefinitely when the officer has responded in part, reached agreement, is negotiating, or has reasonably communicated status (AL-0029, AL-0038).
Designating a request time-intensive requires creating an entry in a confidential pending-request log (AL-0035).
A standard request enters a terminal abandoned state if the requester opts not to pay the estimated fee (AL-0042).

material_negatives.note: SB270 creates no administrative or AG-review appeal path for a records denial. The only statutory consequence of non-response is the rebuttable constructive-denial presumption (AL-0027/0028/0036/0037), which positions the requester to seek judicial relief. Absence of a found administrative appeal is not proof none exists elsewhere.

The Act does not itself prescribe a judicial appeal/enforcement procedure, timeline, or venue. Enforcement historically proceeds by mandamus in circuit court under prior Alabama case law (e.g., the Open Records Act line of cases); that remedy/procedure was intentionally excluded here under the inclusion test (remedy/enforcement-amount) except for the deemed-denial trigger. A dedicated case-law pass is needed for the mandamus standard.

No explicit statewide segregability / 'redact-and-release the non-exempt remainder' mandate. Redaction is contemplated only as a processing-time factor in the standard/time-intensive definitions and as preserved by the savings clause (36-12-43(c)); the duty to release segregable portions is not affirmatively stated in SB270.

No statewide fixed copy rate, per-page ceiling, or itemized fee schedule. Fees are governed only by the 'reasonable fee set by the public officer' soft standard (AL-0039); each officer/municipality sets the actual amount.
No statutory fee-waiver, reduced-fee, or public-interest/indigency provision found in SB270.
No explicit rule governing electronic-record format, native format, or a requester's right to choose format. The Act speaks to copies and inspection generally without a format-selection provision.

No request-triggered or litigation-triggered preservation/legal-hold obligation is created by SB270 (the litigation provision, 36-12-46 / AL-0052, bars using the Act in lieu of discovery rather than imposing a hold). Routine retention schedules are governed separately and excluded.
The statute requires an acknowledgment (AL-0024/0030) but does not prescribe required content or form for the acknowledgment itself.

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to inspection by any person
rules.atomic_rule: All public books and records of a governmental entity must be open during office hours to inspection by any person, and may be fully copied.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: all public books and public records of a governmental entity must be open at all times during office hours to inspection by any person, and may be fully copied or an abstract or memorandum may be prepared from those public books and public records.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.010(1)
rules.notes: Universal-access right. Subject to the long list of statutory confidentiality cross-references opened by the 'Except as otherwise provided' clause, which are not inventoried here.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Access runs to 'any person'; the statute imposes no residency or citizenship condition on who may request public records.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: all public books and public records of a governmental entity must be open at all times during office hours to inspection by any person
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.010(1)
rules.notes: Emitted as a universal-access rule with the shared eligibility key per prompt discipline. The verbatim clause is the 'any person' access grant; 'no residency requirement' is the absence of any residency qualifier anywhere in Chapter 239.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: Access runs to 'any person'; the statute requires no statement of purpose or justification for a request.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: all public books and public records of a governmental entity must be open at all times during office hours to inspection by any person
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.010(1)
rules.notes: Emitted as a universal-access rule with the shared eligibility key. Chapter 239 contains no purpose or use limitation on requests generally (a narrow exception exists at NRS 239.0105 for certain recreational-registration records disclosed only to specified requesters).

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'governmental entity' (includes political subdivisions)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Governmental entity' includes an elected or appointed officer, and any unit of government, of a political subdivision of the State — bringing municipalities within the Act.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: ‘Governmental entity’ means: (a) An elected or appointed officer of this State or of a political subdivision of this State; (b) An institution, board, commission, bureau, council, department, division, authority or other unit of government of this State, including, without limitation, an agency of the Executive Department, or of a political subdivision of this State;
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.005(5)
rules.notes: Coverage definition the platform branches on to determine that a municipal body is subject to Chapter 239. Subsections (c)-(e) also reach certain university/educational/library foundations, omitted here.

rules.legal_concept: Request may be written or oral
rules.atomic_rule: A request to inspect, copy or receive a copy may be made either in writing or orally; the response duty is triggered by either form.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a request from a person
rules.source_language: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after the date on which the person who has legal custody or control of a public book or record of a governmental entity receives a written or oral request from a person to inspect, copy or receive a copy of the public book or record, a governmental entity shall do one of the following, as applicable:
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.0107(1)
rules.notes: Intake must accept oral as well as written requests. For state Executive Department agencies (not municipalities) a prescribed request form exists under NRS 239.008; no equivalent mandatory form binds municipal entities.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after receipt of a request, the entity must allow inspection/copying or provide the copy (or give one of the alternative statutory responses).
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a written or oral request
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from custodian's receipt of request
rules.source_language: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after the date on which the person who has legal custody or control of a public book or record of a governmental entity receives a written or oral request from a person to inspect, copy or receive a copy of the public book or record, a governmental entity shall do one of the following, as applicable: (a) Except as otherwise provided in subsection 2, allow the person to inspect or copy the public book or record or, if the request is for the person to receive a copy of the public book or record, provide such a copy to the person.
rules.notes: 'Not later than the end of the fifth business day' is an outer limit (may respond sooner). One of four responses (a: produce; b: no-custody referral NV-0011; c: extension NV-0008; d: confidential denial NV-0012) must be given within this window. Chapter 239 does not define 'business day' or provide tolling rules. Added 2007; amended 2013, 2019.

rules.legal_concept: Readily available records provided as expeditiously as practicable
rules.atomic_rule: If a record is readily available for inspection or copying, the custodian must allow the requester to inspect, copy or receive a copy as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.trigger: Requested record is readily available for inspection or copying
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as expeditiously as practicable" from receipt of request
rules.source_language: If a public book or record of a governmental entity is readily available for inspection or copying, the person who has legal custody or control of the public book or record shall allow a person who has submitted a request to inspect, copy or receive a copy of a public book or record as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.0107(2)
rules.notes: Soft standard ('as expeditiously as practicable') accelerates production of readily-available records ahead of the 5-business-day outer limit; no numeric value — do not convert to a day count.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of earliest availability date when unable to produce by day five
rules.atomic_rule: If unable to make the record available by the end of the fifth business day, the entity must give the requester written notice of that fact and the earliest date and time the entity reasonably believes the record will be available.
rules.trigger: Entity unable to make record available by end of fifth business day
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes" the record will be available, from the end of the 5th business day
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (d), if the governmental entity is unable to make the public book or record available by the end of the fifth business day after the date on which the person who has legal custody or control of the public book or record received the request: (1) Provide to the person, in writing, notice of the fact that it is unable to make the public book or record available by that date and the earliest date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes the public book or record will be available for the person to inspect or copy or after which a copy of the public book or record will be available to the person.
rules.notes: A required written notice that also sets a self-declared soft future availability date. Config Home structural because the 'reasonably believes' date is a standard the entity applies, not a value the city fills.

rules.legal_concept: Follow-up written explanation and new date if record still unavailable
rules.atomic_rule: If the record is still not available by the date and time the entity previously represented, the entity must provide a written explanation of the reason and a new reasonably-believed availability date and time.
rules.trigger: Record not available by the date/time previously represented under NV-0008
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: new "date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes" availability, from lapse of the previously represented date
rules.source_language: If the public book or record or the copy of the public book or record is not available to the person by that date and time, the governmental entity shall provide to the person, in writing, an explanation of the reason the public book or record is not available and a date and time after which the governmental entity reasonably believes the public book or record will be available for the person to inspect or copy or after which a copy of the public book or record will be available to the person.
rules.notes: Second sentence of the same paragraph as NV-0008; split out as a distinct recurring notice obligation triggered by a missed self-declared date.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable effort to help requester focus the request
rules.atomic_rule: When unable to produce by day five, the entity must make a reasonable effort to assist the requester to focus the request to maximize the likelihood of obtaining the record as expeditiously as possible.
rules.trigger: Entity unable to make record available by end of fifth business day
rules.source_language: (2) Make a reasonable effort to assist the requester to focus the request in such a manner as to maximize the likelihood the requester will be able to inspect, copy or receive a copy of the public book or record as expeditiously as possible.
rules.notes: A duty to assist in narrowing; not a clarification clock. Chapter 239 contains no provision deeming a request abandoned if the requester does not respond.

rules.legal_concept: Written referral when entity lacks custody or control
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity does not have legal custody or control of the record, it must provide written notice of that fact and the name and address of the entity that does have custody or control, if known.
rules.trigger: Entity lacks legal custody or control of the requested record
rules.source_language: If the governmental entity does not have legal custody or control of the public book or record, provide to the person, in writing: (1) Notice of the fact that it does not have legal custody or control of the public book or record; and (2) The name and address of the governmental entity that has legal custody or control of the public book or record, if known.
rules.notes: Routing/referral response; one of the four permitted responses due within the 5-business-day window (NV-0006).

rules.legal_concept: Written denial with citation to confidentiality authority
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity must deny the request because the record (or part) is confidential, it must provide written notice of that fact and a citation to the specific statute or other legal authority making it confidential.
rules.trigger: Entity must deny because the record or part is confidential
rules.source_language: If the governmental entity must deny the person’s request because the public book or record, or a part thereof, is confidential, provide to the person, in writing: (1) Notice of that fact; and (2) A citation to the specific statute or other legal authority that makes the public book or record, or a part thereof, confidential.
rules.notes: Denial response; due within the 5-business-day window. Requires a specific legal citation, not a bare denial.

rules.legal_concept: No denial where confidential information can be redacted or separated
rules.atomic_rule: The entity must not deny a request on the basis that the record contains confidential information if it can redact, delete, conceal or separate (including electronically) the confidential information from the non-confidential information.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains both confidential and non-confidential information
rules.source_language: A governmental entity that has legal custody or control of a public book or record shall not deny a request made pursuant to subsection 1 to inspect or copy or receive a copy of a public book or record on the basis that the requested public book or record contains information that is confidential if the governmental entity can redact, delete, conceal or separate, including, without limitation, electronically, the confidential information from the information included in the public book or record that is not otherwise confidential.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.010(3)
rules.notes: Segregability/partial-disclosure duty; constrains the denial pathway in NV-0012.

rules.legal_concept: Provision of copy in electronic format on request; exceptions
rules.atomic_rule: If requested, the entity must provide a copy in an electronic format by electronic medium, unless the record was neither created nor available electronically, or doing so would give access to proprietary software or require producing non-separable confidential information.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for an electronic-format copy
rules.source_language: If requested, a governmental entity shall provide a copy of a public record in an electronic format by means of an electronic medium. Nothing in this subsection requires a governmental entity to provide a copy of a public record in an electronic format or by means of an electronic medium if: (a) The public record: (1) Was not created or prepared in an electronic format; and (2) Is not available in an electronic format; or (b) Providing the public record in an electronic format or by means of an electronic medium would: (1) Give access to proprietary software; or (2) Require the production of information that is confidential and that cannot be redacted, deleted, concealed or separated from information that is not otherwise confidential.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.010(4)
rules.notes: Requirement plus its conjunctive exceptions kept in one row per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Copy must be provided in the requested medium
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian must not refuse to provide a copy in the requested medium because it has already prepared, or would prefer to provide, the copy in a different medium.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium the custodian would prefer not to use
rules.source_language: An officer, employee or agent of a governmental entity who has legal custody or control of a public record: (a) Shall not refuse to provide a copy of that public record in the medium that is requested because the officer, employee or agent has already prepared or would prefer to provide the copy in a different medium.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.010(5)(a)

rules.legal_concept: Entity must prepare the copy, not the requester
rules.atomic_rule: On request, the custodian must prepare the copy of the record and must not require the requester to prepare the copy himself or herself.
rules.trigger: Requester asks the entity to prepare a copy
rules.source_language: (b) Except as otherwise provided in NRS 239.030, shall, upon request, prepare the copy of the public record and shall not require the person who has requested the copy to prepare the copy himself or herself.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.010(5)(b)
rules.notes: Cross-references NRS 239.030 (certified copies) as an exception.

rules.legal_concept: Furnishing of certified copies on request
rules.atomic_rule: An officer having custody of non-confidential public records must furnish certified copies to any person who requests them and pays or tenders the prescribed copying/certifying fees.
rules.trigger: Person requests certified copies of non-confidential records and tenders fees
rules.source_language: Every officer having custody of public records, the contents of which are not declared by law to be confidential, shall furnish copies certified to be correct to any person who requests them and pays or tenders such fees as may be prescribed for the service of copying and certifying.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.030
rules.notes: Certified-copy production path; distinct from ordinary copies in that fee tender is an express precondition (see NV-0018).

rules.legal_concept: Payment or tender of fees as precondition to certified copies
rules.atomic_rule: For certified copies, the requester must pay or tender the prescribed copying and certifying fees as a condition of the officer's duty to furnish them.
rules.trigger: Request for certified copies
rules.source_language: shall furnish copies certified to be correct to any person who requests them and pays or tenders such fees as may be prescribed for the service of copying and certifying.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.030
rules.notes: Payment gate is expressed only for certified copies under NRS 239.030; Chapter 239 authorizes no general advance deposit or prepayment before search for ordinary copies.

rules.legal_concept: County recorder production of stored item within three working days
rules.atomic_rule: When a county recorder receives a request for a particular item that has been removed to storage, the recorder must produce a microfilmed copy or the original within three working days.
rules.trigger: County recorder receives a request for an item stored under NRS 239.015(1)
rules.clock_spec: 3 working-days from county recorder's receipt of request
rules.source_language: If a county recorder receives a request for a particular item which has been stored pursuant to subsection 1, the county recorder shall produce a microfilmed copy of such item or the original within 3 working days.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.015(2)
rules.notes: Record/entity-specific deadline applicable to county recorders for stored items; distinct from the general 5-business-day window. Uses 'working days' (vs. 'business days' elsewhere).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee limited to actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may charge a fee for a copy, but the fee must not exceed the actual cost to provide the copy unless a specific statute or regulation sets the fee.
rules.trigger: Entity provides a copy of a public record
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of providing the copy
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.052(1)
rules.notes: Permission to charge plus its actual-cost ceiling kept in one row. City sets the operative per-copy rate under the actual-cost ceiling; a more specific statute/regulation can override the ceiling. Added 1997; amended 2013.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'actual cost' (excludes overhead/labor)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Actual cost' means direct cost of providing the copy (ink, toner, paper, media, postage) and excludes any cost the entity incurs regardless of whether a copy is requested.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: ‘Actual cost’ means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.005(1)
rules.notes: Definition the fee engine branches on: the 'regardless of request' exclusion bars charging for staff/labor time and overhead. Reinforced by 2019 SB287, which also repealed the former extraordinary-use personnel fee (NRS 239.055).

rules.legal_concept: No fee where statute/regulation requires free copy
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity must not charge a fee for a copy if a specific statute or regulation requires it to provide the copy without charge.
rules.trigger: A specific statute or regulation requires the copy to be provided free
rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.052(1)
rules.notes: Third sentence of NRS 239.052(1); a fee-suppression branch triggered by other free-copy mandates (e.g., NV-0027).

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver by written policy
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may waive all or part of a copy fee if it adopts a written waiver policy and posts a legible sign or notice of the policy's terms at each office providing copies.
rules.trigger: Entity has adopted a written waiver policy and posted notice
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may waive all or a portion of a charge or fee for a copy of a public record if the governmental entity: (a) Adopts a written policy to waive all or a portion of a charge or fee for a copy of a public record; and (b) Posts, in a conspicuous place at each office in which the governmental entity provides copies of public records, a legible sign or notice that states the terms of the policy.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.052(2)
rules.notes: Waiver is discretionary and conditioned on a posted written policy.

rules.legal_concept: Law library copy fee ceiling of 50 cents per page
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for a copy of a record in the custody of a governmental law library must not exceed 50 cents per page.
rules.trigger: Copy provided from a record in a governmental law library's custody
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.50/page
rules.source_language: The fee for providing a copy of a public book or record in the custody of a law library operated by a governmental entity must not exceed 50 cents per page.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.052(4)
rules.notes: Record/entity-specific per-page ceiling; city law library sets the operative rate up to $0.50/page.

rules.legal_concept: Additional fee for administrative-proceeding transcript
rules.atomic_rule: For a copy of a certified-court-reporter transcript of an administrative proceeding, the entity must charge, on top of actual medium cost, a per-page fee equal to the court reporter's contract per-page fee, and remit that amount to the reporter.
rules.trigger: Person requests a copy of a transcribed administrative-proceeding transcript
rules.clock_spec: fixed: court reporter's contract per-page fee + actual medium cost
rules.source_language: If a person requests a copy of a transcript of an administrative proceeding that has been transcribed by a certified court reporter, a governmental entity shall charge, in addition to the actual cost of the medium in which the copy of the transcript is provided, a fee for each page provided which is equal in amount to the fee per page charged by the court reporter for the copy of the transcript, as set forth in the contract between the governmental entity and the court reporter.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.053(1)
rules.notes: Special-record fee; the per-page value is fixed by the entity-reporter contract, not freely set by the city. An exception to the general actual-cost ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Additional fee for geographic information system data
rules.atomic_rule: A fee for information from a geographic information system may include, in addition to actual medium cost, the reasonable costs of data gathering/entry, database maintenance, hardware, software, quality control, and consultation with personnel.
rules.trigger: Request for information from a geographic information system
rules.source_language: A fee for the provision of information from a geographic information system may include, in addition to the actual cost of the medium in which the information is provided, the reasonable costs related to: (a) The gathering and entry of data into the system; (b) Maintenance and updating of the database of the system; (c) Hardware; (d) Software; (e) Quality control; and (f) Consultation with personnel of the governmental entity.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.054(1)
rules.notes: Special-record fee permitting recovery of 'reasonable costs' beyond actual cost for GIS data — a statutory exception to the actual-cost ceiling; no numeric value (soft-standard).

rules.legal_concept: Certified copies for VA benefit eligibility furnished without charge
rules.atomic_rule: When a public record copy is required by the federal Department of Veterans Affairs to determine benefit eligibility, the custodian must provide a certified copy without charge to the applicant, their representative, or the VA.
rules.trigger: Copy required by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs for benefit-eligibility determination
rules.source_language: Whenever a copy of any public record is required by the Department of Veterans Affairs to be used in determining the eligibility of any person to participate in benefits made available by the Department of Veterans Affairs, the official charged with the custody of such public record shall, without charge, provide the applicant for the benefit or any person acting on behalf of the applicant or the representative of the Department of Veterans Affairs with a certified copy or copies of such records.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.020
rules.notes: Requester/purpose-specific fee exemption (a mandatory free-copy statute that triggers NV-0022).

rules.legal_concept: Application to district court on denial, delay, or fee dispute
rules.atomic_rule: If a request is denied or unreasonably delayed, or the requester believes the fee is excessive or improper, the requester may apply to the district court in the county where the record is located for an order permitting inspection/copying, requiring a copy, or granting fee relief.
rules.trigger: Request denied or unreasonably delayed, or fee believed excessive or improper
rules.source_language: If a request for inspection, copying or copies of a public book or record open to inspection and copying is denied or unreasonably delayed or if a person who requests a copy of a public book or record believes that the fee charged by the governmental entity for providing the copy of the public book or record is excessive or improper, the requester may apply to the district court in the county in which the book or record is located for an order: (a) Permitting the requester to inspect or copy the book or record; (b) Requiring the person who has legal custody or control of the public book or record to provide a copy to the requester; or (c) Providing relief relating to the amount of the fee, as applicable.
rules.source_authority: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.011(1)
rules.notes: Judicial-review path (namespaced appeal.judicial.*). 'Unreasonably delayed' is the soft trigger; Nevada has no fixed deemed-denial day count and no internal administrative appeal stage. Priority-of-matter and cost/attorney-fee recovery provisions (NRS 239.011(2)-(3)) are remedy details excluded from processing config.

rules.legal_concept: Court application to access records held 30+ years; rebuttable presumption
rules.atomic_rule: For a record held in governmental custody or control for at least 30 years, a person may apply to district court for an order to inspect or copy it notwithstanding a confidentiality declaration, with a rebuttable presumption of entitlement (subject to stated exceptions).
rules.trigger: Record has been in governmental custody or control for at least 30 years (or, for records about a natural person, the later of 30 years or that person's death)
