rules.source_language: notwithstanding any provision of law that has declared a public book or record, or a part thereof, to be confidential, if a public book or record has been in the legal custody or control of one or more governmental entities for at least 30 years, a person may apply to the district court of the county in which the governmental entity that currently has legal custody or control of the public book or record is located for an order directing that governmental entity to allow the person to inspect or copy the public book or record, or a part thereof. ... There is a rebuttable presumption that a person who applies for an order as described in subsection 1 is entitled to inspect or copy the public book or record, or a part thereof, that the person seeks to inspect or copy.
rules.notes: Distinct judicial path for aged records (namespaced appeal.judicial.*). Exceptions in subsection 3 (gaming/cannabis-confidential records under NRS 463.120/678A.470, and confidential crime-victim personal information) not automated here. Amended 2025.

structural_branches.description: NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(1): a required written notice, given when the entity cannot produce by day five, declaring the earliest reasonably-believed availability date — a distinct processing stage that pauses production against a self-set soft date (NV-0008).
NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(1): a recurring follow-up written explanation plus a new availability date whenever a previously represented date lapses (NV-0009).
NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(2): a mandatory 'reasonable effort' to help the requester focus the request when production cannot occur by day five (NV-0010).
NRS 239.0107(1)(b): a referral branch — written notice of no custody plus name/address of the entity that has the record (NV-0011).
NRS 239.0107(1)(d): the confidential-denial branch requiring written notice with a specific legal citation (NV-0012).
NRS 239.010(3): mandatory partial-disclosure/redaction path barring denial of a record that mixes confidential and non-confidential content (NV-0013).
NRS 239.010(4): electronic-format production branch with its four statutory exceptions (NV-0014).
NRS 239.011(1): the sole external review path — district-court application on denial, unreasonable delay, or fee dispute; Nevada has no internal administrative appeal stage (NV-0028).
NRS 239.0115: a separate district-court path to reach records held 30+ years, carrying a rebuttable presumption of access and enumerated exceptions (NV-0029).
NRS 239.020: a mandatory free-certified-copy branch for federal VA benefit-eligibility determinations (NV-0027).

material_negatives.note: No separate acknowledgment/receipt step distinct from the substantive response. NRS 239.0107(1) sets a single 5-business-day window within which the entity must produce, refer, extend, or deny; there is no earlier statutory duty merely to acknowledge receipt.

No statutory authority in Chapter 239 for an advance deposit or prepayment before search/production of ordinary copies. Fee tender is expressly required only for certified copies (NRS 239.030, NV-0018).

Chapter 239 draws no distinction between commercial and non-commercial requesters and creates no purpose-based fee tier; the actual-cost ceiling (NRS 239.052) applies without regard to requester purpose.

No fee is authorized for staff time, labor, or overhead. The 'actual cost' definition (NRS 239.005(1)) excludes costs incurred regardless of a request, and 2019 SB287 repealed the former extraordinary-use-of-personnel fee (NRS 239.055). Absence of a labor charge is affirmative, not merely unfound.

No fixed constructive/deemed-denial trigger (no 'silence for N days = denial'). The only silence-related trigger is the soft 'unreasonably delayed' standard for a district-court application under NRS 239.011(1) (NV-0028).

No internal or administrative appeal stage exists in Chapter 239; the exclusive review mechanism is a district-court application (NRS 239.011). Emitted as a negative so it does not falsely merge with other states' internal-appeal stages.

Chapter 239 does not define 'business day' or 'working day', nor does it provide tolling, holiday-exclusion, or day-counting rules for the 5-business-day (NRS 239.0107) or 3-working-day (NRS 239.015(2)) periods. Later pass may need general NRS time-computation rules or municipal practice.

No provision deeming a request abandoned or closed if the requester fails to respond to a narrowing/clarification effort. NRS 239.0107(1)(c)(2) imposes a duty to assist but attaches no requester-side deadline or abandonment consequence.

Chapter 239 contains no preservation/litigation hold triggered by the making of a records request or by an appeal on that request. (General records-retention schedules exist under NRS 239.051-239.125 but are routine retention, excluded.)
